evidence.title: Sylvan Twp: Notice of Resolution 26-05
evidence.publisher: The Sun Times News (publishing Sylvan Township's official notice)
evidence.supports: Official township notice confirms Resolution 26-05's operative scope explicitly names data centers (among other uses), its 12-month original term effective immediately from the July 14, 2026 adoption, and the six-month cap on any future extensions.
evidence.quote: Resolution 26-05 approves a 12-month temporary moratorium on the acceptance and/or processing of any applications for data centers, high energy users, power generation facilities and similar uses within Sylvan Township... Future extensions shall not exceed six (6) month increments... The resolution is effective immediately.

decisions.notes: SECTOR_CHECK resolved: the township's own official notice of Resolution 26-05 confirms 'data centers' is explicit, named operative scope (alongside high-energy users and power-generation facilities), not a trigger mention -- the prior pass had left sectors as general-only despite the row's own legal_basis/current_status text already saying the same thing. sectors corrected to add data_center. duration_days=365 for the DURATION_MISMATCH context (not itself flagged on this row, but present in the same duration text) is confirmed correct following the same convention as mi-elmwood-township-tuscola-county-2026: it reflects the currently operative Resolution 26-05's own original 12-month term (confirmed 'effective immediately' from adoption, with the notice's own extension-cap language matching the row's text), not the earlier, now-superseded Ordinance 26-01's 180-day term that the deterministic check matched first.

evidence.title: Utica Council extends moratorium on data centers while attorneys draft ordinance
evidence.supports: Confirms the July 14, 2026 extension vote but explicitly states no effective date or duration figure was given at the meeting.
evidence.quote: Utica City Council voted on July 14 to extend a six‑month moratorium on the establishment of data storage facilities and data centers in the city while legal staff review court decisions and ordinances from other municipalities... No ordinance number or effective date beyond the extension was provided at the meeting; council members said staff will return with draft language once the legal landscape is clearer.

decisions.notes: EXTENDED_NO_END_DATE not resolved: the only detailed account of the extension vote explicitly states neither an ordinance/resolution number nor an effective date/duration figure was given at the meeting, and the row's own original date_enacted_iso is already only month-precision ('2026-01'), so even a computed estimate would rest on two unconfirmed dates. Left current_end_date_iso blank rather than compound two uncertainties into a fabricated date.

current_end_date_iso.reason: Township minutes confirm a six-month extension was adopted at the Aug. 17, 2026 meeting; since the moratorium's original adoption date is itself unconfirmed (date_enacted_iso is already blank on this row), this is computed as six months forward from the one confirmed date available (the extension's own adoption date), which also matches the row's own prior estimate ('to about February 2027').

evidence.title: Wisner Twp. Extends Data Center Moratorium, Moves Ahead with Cemetery Fence Removal
evidence.supports: Confirms the board voted unanimously by roll call to extend the data-center moratorium for an additional six months at its August 17, 2026 meeting.
evidence.quote: WISNER TWP. — The Wisner Township Board extended its data center moratorium for another six months... during its Aug. 17 meeting... Valentine moved to extend the moratorium for an additional six months, with support from Reese. Freed, Mulligan, Valentine, Reese and MacFarlane each voted in favor during a roll call vote.

decisions.notes: EXTENDED_NO_END_DATE partially resolved: unlike Brandon/Dexter/Genoa (where the ORIGINAL adoption date is known, allowing a sequential 'original term + extension' computation), Wisner's original adoption date could not be found in this pass or the row's prior research (jurisdiction is listed 'undated'), so this computes six months forward from the one confirmed date (the extension's own Aug. 17, 2026 adoption), which understates the true end date if the extension (as with the other townships) runs from the original term's own expiration rather than from the extension's adoption date. Confidence set low to reflect that double uncertainty; flagging for a future pass to locate the original ordinance/resolution.
